## Statement
For admissible inputs of [[alg-fixed-point-iteration]] with budget $N\in\mathbb N_0$, every entered iterate belongs to $X$. The procedure uses at most $N$ updates and $N+1$ fixed-point residual evaluations and returns one of its stated statuses. Termination is in the model where each map evaluation, metric evaluation and comparison returns in finite time. These counts specify outer procedure operations and give no bound on the internal cost of evaluating the supplied map or metric.

## Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The algorithm's metric space, self-map, initial point, tolerance and finite budget, and returning evaluation primitives.
[F1] [[alg-fixed-point-iteration]] evaluates its residual once at each entered index, tests tolerance before budget, returns at index $N$ if tolerance fails, and updates only when $k<N$.

## Proof
1.1 Initially $x_0\in X$. If an update is made from $x_k\in X$, the self-map condition gives $x_{k+1}=G(x_k)\in X$. Induction proves membership of every entered iterate. [given, F1, induction]
2.1 A continuing pass advances its index by one. At index $N$, either the residual test returns or the budget test returns before another update. Thus the entered indices form an initial segment of $0,\ldots,N$, with at most $N+1$ residual evaluations and $N$ updates. Every pass contains finitely many returning primitives, so the procedure terminates with a stated status. This includes $N=0$. [F1, step 1.1, induction] ∎

The iteration format is consistent with [FNC §4.2](https://fncbook.com/fixed-point/); the precise local counts are proved above. This result may justify the algorithm through justified_by, without a reverse deps edge. ## Statement
For admissible inputs of [[alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals]] with budget $N\in\mathbb N_0$, every entered iterate lies in $U$. The procedure makes at most $N$ correction calls, at most $N$ accepted updates, and at most $N+1$ explicit outer residual evaluations. It returns a stated residual, singular-Jacobian, invalid-trial or budget status. Termination is in the exact-arithmetic model where residual and Jacobian evaluations, domain decisions and correction calls return in finite time. No convergence, tolerance-attainment or backend complexity claim follows.

## Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The algorithm's admissible inputs and returning primitives.
[F1] [[alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals]] evaluates $F(x_k)$ once at an entered index, checks residual and budget before correction, and accepts an update only after checking membership in $U$.

## Proof
1.1 The initial point lies in $U$. A failed trial returns the current point; an accepted trial becomes the next iterate only after its membership test succeeds. Induction proves membership of all entered iterates. [given, F1, induction]
2.1 The entered indices form an initial segment of $0,\ldots,N$. At $k=N$ the residual or budget branch returns before a correction. Each earlier index permits one correction call and at most one accepted update. Consequently there are at most $N+1$ explicit residual evaluations, $N$ correction calls and $N$ updates. Singular or invalid-trial returns only shorten this execution. The finitely many returning primitives therefore terminate with a stated status, including when $N=0$. [F1, step 1.1, induction] ∎

## Statement
For admissible inputs of either cited SCF iteration with finite budget $N$, there are at most $N$ updates and $N+1$ fixed-point residual tests. Under returning spectrum, response, metric and comparison primitives, the procedure terminates with a stated residual, gap, eigensolver or budget status. This is a work/status bound and does not assert contraction, convergence or tolerance attainment.

## Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** Either algorithm's admissible inputs and returning primitives.
[F1] [[alg-undamped-scf-with-gap-and-residual-status]] checks the spectrum/gap, then its residual, then the budget, and updates only at indices below $N$.
[F2] [[alg-relaxed-density-mixing-with-finite-budget]] uses the same index and stopping order for its relaxed residual, with earlier gap/eigensolver returns allowed.

## Proof
1.1 In either loop the entered indices form an initial segment of $0,\ldots,N$. Each entered index permits at most one residual test. Index $N$ returns before an update, and every earlier continuing index makes one update. Induction gives at most $N+1$ residual tests and $N$ updates. Earlier failures shorten the execution. Each pass contains finitely many returning primitives, proving termination with a stated status. [given, F1, F2, induction] ∎
